title: Noun gender and number
description: Masculine and feminine nouns, the three main endings, and regular plurals.
objectives: Identify the gender of most nouns from their ending.
Form regular plurals of nouns in -o, -a and -e.
Recognise nouns that do not change in the plural.

blocks.text: Every Italian noun is either masculine or feminine — even nouns for objects and ideas. The gender decides which article and which adjective forms go with the noun, so always learn a noun together with its article: *il gatto*, *la casa*.

blocks.caption: Gender by ending
rows: il gatto, il libro, il bosco
la casa, la mela, la luna
il fiore, il cane (m); la notte, la chiave (f)
la città, la felicità, la virtù
il film, lo sport, il bar

blocks.title: Common exceptions
blocks.text: *la mano* (hand) is feminine despite -o. *il problema*, *il papà* and *il poeta* are masculine despite -a. Shortened words keep the gender of the full word: *la foto* (fotografia), *la radio*, *la moto*.

blocks.title: Natural gender
blocks.text: For people and many animals, gender follows sex where a pair exists: *il ragazzo / la ragazza*, *il nonno / la nonna*, *il gatto / la gatta*.

blocks.caption: Plural endings
rows: il fiore → i fiori; la notte → le notti

blocks.title: Invariable nouns
blocks.text: These do not change in the plural: nouns with a stressed final vowel (*la città → le città, il caffè → i caffè*); nouns ending in a consonant (*il film → i film*); one-syllable nouns (*il re → i re*); shortened words (*la foto → le foto*). Only the article shows the number.

examples.note: mano is feminine: la mano, piccola.

exercises.explanation: Masculine -o → -i.
Feminine -a → -e.
Nouns in -e make their plural in -i, whatever their gender.

mistakes.message: notte ends in -e, so its plural ends in -i (even though it is feminine): le notti.

exercises.explanation: Nouns with a stressed final vowel do not change: le città.

mistakes.message: città ends in a stressed (accented) vowel, so it is invariable: le città.

exercises.explanation: la mano is a common exception: feminine despite -o. Plural: le mani.

exercises.prompt: *fiore* ends in -e. What does that tell you about its gender?
options: Nothing certain: -e nouns can be masculine or feminine
exercises.answer: Nothing certain: -e nouns can be masculine or feminine
exercises.explanation: il fiore is masculine, la notte is feminine. Learn every -e noun with its article.

exercises.prompt: Match each singular to its plural.
exercises.explanation: -o → -i, -a → -e, -e → -i; one-syllable re is invariable.

summary: -o: usually masculine; -a: usually feminine; -e: either — learn the article.
Invariable: final stressed vowel, final consonant, one syllable, shortened words.
Exceptions to remember: la mano, il problema, il papà.

title: The definite article
description: il, lo, l', la, i, gli, le — choosing the article from the noun's gender, number and first letters.
objectives: Choose the correct definite article for any noun whose gender you know.
Apply the lo/gli rule for s + consonant, z, gn, ps, x, y.
Use l' before vowels and know its plural (gli or le).

blocks.text: The definite article (the) agrees in gender and number with the noun, and its form also depends on the sound at the start of the **next word**.

blocks.caption: Definite articles
rows: most consonants: il gatto → i gatti
s + consonant, z, gn, ps, pn, x, y: lo zaino → gli zaini; lo specchio → gli specchi
a consonant: la casa → le case

blocks.title: The article depends on the next word
blocks.text: The choice is made by the word immediately after the article, which may be an adjective: *lo zio* but *il mio zio*; *l'amico* but *il vecchio amico*.

blocks.title: Feminine plural never elides
blocks.text: In the plural, use *le* before every feminine noun, including those beginning with a vowel: *le api, le arance* (not *l'api*).
Italian uses the definite article more than English does:

items: With general statements: *Il miele è dolce* = Honey is sweet.
With categories you like or dislike: *Amo i gatti* = I love cats.
With possessives: *il mio libro* (see the possessives lesson).
Not with names of people: *Marco*, not *il Marco* (except in some regional speech).

examples.note: gli: plural of lo and of masculine l'.
General statement: Italian uses the article.

exercises.explanation: Masculine nouns beginning with z take lo: lo zaino.

mistakes.message: il is used before most consonants, but z (like s + consonant, gn, ps) requires lo.

exercises.explanation: Before a vowel, lo elides to l': l'albero.
The feminine plural article is always le, even before a vowel.

mistakes.message: l' is singular only. The feminine plural is always le: le api.

exercises.prompt: Give the plural with its article.
exercises.explanation: il → i; lo → gli; masculine l' → gli; la → le; feminine l' → le.

exercises.prompt: *zio* takes *lo* (lo zio). Which article goes in: ___ vecchio zio?
exercises.explanation: The article is chosen by the word that immediately follows it: vecchio begins with v, so il vecchio zio, even though lo zio. (With a possessive and a singular family noun the article is normally dropped: mio zio — see the possessives lesson.)
General statements use the article in Italian: le api, il miele.

summary: Masculine: il/i (most consonants), lo/gli (s + consonant, z, gn, ps…), l'/gli (vowel).
The article is chosen by the word right after it.
General statements and categories take the article: Il miele è dolce.

title: The indefinite article; c'è and ci sono
description: un, uno, una, un'; saying 'there is' and 'there are'.
objectives: Choose un, uno, una or un' correctly.
Say what there is somewhere with c'è and ci sono.

blocks.caption: Indefinite articles (a / an)
rows: s + consonant, z, gn, ps, x, y

blocks.title: The parallel with the definite article
blocks.text: Wherever the definite article is *lo*, the indefinite is *uno* (lo zaino / uno zaino). Before a masculine vowel, *l'* corresponds to *un* without an apostrophe (l'albero / un albero).
*c'è* (= *ci è*) means 'there is'; *ci sono* means 'there are'. The verb agrees with what follows.

items: *C'è un gatto in giardino.* = There is a cat in the garden.
*Ci sono tre gatti in giardino.* = There are three cats in the garden.
Past (imperfetto): *c'era / c'erano* = there was / there were — as in *C'era una volta…* (Once upon a time there was…).

blocks.text: The indefinite article has no plural, but *di* + the definite article gives the meaning 'some': *dei gatti* (some cats), *degli alberi* (some trees), *delle mele* (some apples). These are the partitive article: *di* contracted with the definite article (*di + i = dei, di + gli = degli, di + le = delle*; in the singular *del pane, della farina* = some bread, some flour, with uncountable nouns). The contractions themselves are covered in the lesson on [[articulated-prepositions|articulated prepositions]]. The partitive is optional: *Ho comprato mele* and *Ho comprato delle mele* are both correct, and in negative sentences it is usually omitted: *Non ho comprato mele*. *alcuni/alcune* + plural and *un po' di* + singular are common alternatives.

examples.it: Ho un cane e una gatta.
examples.en: I have a (male) dog and a (female) cat.
There is a squirrel in the tree.
There is a bee on the flower.

examples.it: Ci sono molte stelle in cielo.
examples.en: There are many stars in the sky.

examples.note: un before a masculine vowel, no apostrophe.

exercises.explanation: z requires uno (compare lo zaino).
Feminine before a vowel: un'isola.
Masculine before a vowel: un orso — never un'.

mistakes.message: un' is only for feminine nouns. orso is masculine: un orso.

exercises.prompt: Complete with c'è or ci sono.
exercises.text: In giardino {0} un albero. Sull'albero {1} due uccelli.
exercises.explanation: c'è + singular, ci sono + plural.

exercises.answer: There is a bee on the flower.
accept: There's a bee on the flower
exercises.explanation: c'è = there is; un'ape = a bee; sul fiore = on the flower.
ci sono + plural noun.

summary: un (most masculine nouns, including vowels), uno (s + consonant, z…), una (feminine consonant), un' (feminine vowel).
c'è + singular = there is; ci sono + plural = there are; c'era = there was.

title: Spelling changes and irregular plurals
description: Plurals of -ca/-ga, -co/-go, -cia/-gia and -io, and the common irregular nouns.
objectives: Form plurals with the spelling adjustments for hard c and g.
Know which plural patterns are rules and which are only tendencies.
Learn the high-frequency irregular nouns: uomo, uovo, braccio, mano.

blocks.title: Feminine -ca/-ga → -che/-ghe
blocks.text: The h keeps the hard sound in the plural: *la mucca → le mucche*, *la barca → le barche*, *la tartaruga → le tartarughe*.

sections.heading: -co and -go: a tendency, not a rule

blocks.title: It depends on the stress
blocks.text: If the stress falls on the second-to-last syllable, -co/-go usually become -chi/-ghi: *il BO-sco → i boschi*, *il LA-go → i laghi*, *il GIO-co → i giochi*. If it falls earlier, they usually become -ci/-gi: *il ME-di-co → i medici*, *sim-PA-ti-co → simpatici*.

blocks.title: Exceptions
blocks.text: *l'amico → gli amici*, *il nemico → i nemici*, *il greco → i greci* are stressed on the second-to-last syllable but still take -ci. Learn these individually.

blocks.caption: Plurals with i
rows: l'arancia → le arance; la spiaggia → le spiagge
la camicia → le camicie; la valigia → le valigie
il figlio → i figli; l'occhio → gli occhi

blocks.caption: Common irregular plurals
rows: body parts: also il dito → le dita, il labbro → le labbra
collective noun, always singular: la gente è…

examples.en: The cows are in the meadow.

examples.it: Nei boschi ci sono molti funghi.
examples.en: There are many mushrooms in the woods.

examples.it: Il gatto ha gli occhi verdi.

exercises.explanation: -ca → -che, always.

mistakes.message: In barce the c before e would be soft, as in English 'church'. Keep the hard k sound with h: barche.

exercises.explanation: amico is an exception to the -co → -chi tendency.

mistakes.message: amico is a well-known exception: gli amici.

exercises.explanation: GIO-co is stressed on the second-to-last syllable: giochi.

exercises.prompt: Write the plural with its article.
exercises.explanation: uomini (irregular), le uova (feminine plural), le mani, zii (stressed ì), spiagge (-gia after a consonant).

options: -ca always becomes -che, but -co becomes -chi or -ci depending largely on stress.
-ca and -co both always keep the hard sound with h.
exercises.answer: -ca always becomes -che, but -co becomes -chi or -ci depending largely on stress.
exercises.explanation: The -ca rule has no exceptions; the -co pattern is a tendency with exceptions (amico, medico…).

exercises.prompt: Translate: The cat has green eyes.
exercises.answer: Il gatto ha gli occhi verdi.
exercises.explanation: occhio → occhi (unstressed -io → -i); gli before a vowel.

summary: -cia/-gia: -ce/-ge after a consonant, -cie/-gie after a vowel (tendency).
